subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Holes: The Missing Electron Illusion
description: A fast breakdown of Holes: The Missing Electron Illusion for builders.

hook.text: Remove an electron from silicon and its empty seat moves through the crystal like a bubble.

buildup.text: Neighboring electrons hop into the vacancy. The hole appears to drift the opposite way.

discovery.text: Holes behave as positive charge carriers. Engineers treat them as real particles in math.

twist.text: In P-type silicon, holes outnumber electrons. Current flows mostly via these ghost particles.

climax.text: Transistors rely on both electrons and holes moving in opposite directions simultaneously.

punchline.text: A missing electron becomes a positive particle — physics loves a good illusion.

quiz.question: What is a 'hole' in semiconductor physics?
options: A physical gap in the crystal lattice
An absence of an electron that behaves like a positive charge carrier
A region of high resistance inside the semiconductor
